title: Graham Cracker Buttermilk Pancakes
changes_from_base: Graham cracker crumbs and a little cornmeal replace half the flour, for a nutty, wholemeal flavour.
summary: Buttermilk pancakes given a toasty flavour from crushed graham crackers and a touch of cornmeal.
equipment: nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle
wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: whole graham crackers, crushed to crumbs (about 240 ml)
fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 93°C, spray the wire rack with oil and set it on its tray.

steps.title: Whisk Dry
steps.text: Whisk the crushed crumbs from 8 graham crackers with 142 g plain flour, 2 tbsp cornmeal, 2 tbsp caster sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda and ½ tsp fine salt.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Whisk 480 ml buttermilk, 60 ml soured cream, 2 eggs and 42 g melted butter in another bowl, pour this into a well in the dry mix and stir gently until just combined and lumpy, then rest the batter 10 min.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat 1-2 tsp vegetable oil in a 30 cm non-stick pan over medium heat, wipe out leaving a thin film, then portion 60 ml batter in 4 places and cook until the edges set, the base turns golden and bubbles begin to break, 2-3 min.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook until golden, a further 1-2 min.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Serve straight away or keep warm on the rack, repeating with the rest of the batter and using the remaining oil as needed.

tips: Crush the graham crackers finely so they blend smoothly into the batter.
Don't overmix once the wet and dry ingredients meet - a lumpy batter makes for fluffier pancakes.
Keep cooked pancakes on a warm rack in the oven so the whole batch stays warm together.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
